# 2 · Author & Validate the Codebook {.unnumbered}

The **Codebook** (UIAO_151) is the single source of truth for what an OrgPath
*is*: which semantic facets exist, which directory slot each occupies, and
which values are legal. Every downstream step — assessment, drift
classification, device writeback — validates against it. Get this right first.

Executable SSOT: `src/uiao/canon/data/orgpath/codebook.yaml`
Schema: `src/uiao/schemas/orgpath/codebook.schema.json` (v2.0.0)
Narrative canon: `UIAO_151`.

## 2.1 The 15-facet model

Model C (ADR-078) binds each facet to exactly one
`onPremisesExtensionAttribute` slot on the directory object. Ten named facets
are canonical; slots 11–15 are reserved for tenant extension.

| Slot | Facet | Kind | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `extensionAttribute1` | `region` | enumerated | Geographic / cloud region anchor |
| `extensionAttribute2` | `department` | enumerated | Top-level department |
| `extensionAttribute3` | `division` | enumerated | Division within department |
| `extensionAttribute4` | `role` | enumerated | Job role / persona |
| `extensionAttribute5` | `cost_center` | enumerated | Cost center |
| `extensionAttribute6` | `classification` | enumerated | Worker classification |
| `extensionAttribute7` | `hire_date` | typed (date) | Lifecycle start |
| `extensionAttribute8` | `term_date` | typed (date) | Lifecycle end |
| `extensionAttribute9` | `clearance_level` | enumerated | Clearance / trust tier |
| `extensionAttribute10` | `account_type` | enumerated | Human / service / privileged |
| `extensionAttribute11–15` | *(reserved)* | reserved | Tenant-specific extension |

::: {.callout-warning}
The **slot assignments of the 10 named facets must not change** without a
superseding ADR — they are part of the canonical contract that dynamic groups,
Administrative Units, and Conditional Access compose against. You tune the
*enumerations*, not the *slots*.
:::

## 2.2 Facet kinds

| Kind | Validation rule | Drift if violated |
|---|---|---|
| **enumerated** | Value must be in the facet's closed `enumeration` list | Value Drift (`DRIFT-SEMANTIC`, P2) |
| **typed** | Value must match `value_type` (e.g. `date`) and optional `value_pattern` | Format Drift (P1, never auto-fixed) |
| **reserved** | No semantics declared; cannot be written until promoted | Writes skipped silently |

Lifecycle dates (`hire_date`, `term_date`) are **typed** because dates can't be
enumerated; everything else closed-world is **enumerated**.

## 2.3 What you tune (and what you don't)

**Tune:** the `enumeration` lists of the named facets to match your real
organization. The shipped values are federal-IT defaults (e.g. `region` ships
`NCR, EASTUS, WESTUS, CENTRAL, EMEA, APAC, LATAM`). Add, rename, or remove
values so they reflect your actual regions, departments, divisions, roles,
cost centers, classifications, clearance levels, and account types.

**Don't tune:** slot bindings, facet names, or `kind` of the named facets
without an ADR. To use a reserved slot (11–15), declare its facet semantics via
a governed PR first — the engine refuses to write a slot with no declared
meaning.

### Anatomy of an enumerated facet

```yaml
facets:
  region:
    attribute: extensionAttribute1
    description: >-
      Geographic or cloud region where the principal is administratively
      anchored.
    kind: enumerated
    enumeration:
      - { value: NCR,     description: National Capital Region }
      - { value: EASTUS,  description: Eastern United States }
      # … add/replace with YOUR regions …
```

### Deprecating a value safely

To retire an enumeration value without orphaning principals that still carry
it, mark the replacement so the engine can auto-reassign (Phantom handling):

```yaml
      - { value: OLDREGION, description: Legacy region, replaced_by: EASTUS }
```

## 2.4 Validate

The Codebook must pass schema **and** integrity validation (slot uniqueness,
enumeration well-formedness) before you trust any later step:

```bash
# Validate the canonical shipped Codebook
uiao orgtree validate codebook

# Validate a working copy before promoting it
uiao orgtree validate codebook --data ./my-codebook.yaml
```

A pass prints a one-line summary, e.g.:

```
PASS codebook (UIAO_151) — 10 named facets + 5 reserved slots;
  46 enumerated values; model=C; adoption_tier_min=3
```

A failure prints the specific violation and exits non-zero — wire this into CI
so a malformed Codebook can never merge.

## 2.5 How the Codebook drives the rest

- **Assessment** (Guide 3) validates every AD-derived value against the
  enumeration; unmapped values become *findings*, not silent writes.
- **Governance** (Guide 4) classifies any tenant value outside the Codebook as
  drift, severity by facet kind.
- **Writeback** (Guides 5–6) refuses to write reserved facets and skips values
  that would land as drift.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Promotion discipline

`codebook.yaml` is governed canon. In a real deployment you keep your
tenant-tuned enumerations under change control and promote edits via a reviewed
PR — never hand-edit the in-tenant state to match an unreviewed Codebook. The
Codebook leads; the tenant follows.
:::
